> Two concrete findings strengthen the “improve and reuse” direction, but rule out using it unchanged:
>
> - The external `ITask` interface is already small (`Start`, `Read`, `Cancel`) and worth preserving conceptually.
> - Its worker dispatch currently rejects specialized worker identities unless their grain type is literally `IWorker`; `IGroupChat` therefore cannot cleanly participate, even before its methods throw.
> - The operation ledger already models prepared/dispatched/completed/uncertain external effects—valuable for MCP tool calls—but nothing uses or tests it yet.
>
> So there is useful implementation to salvage, alongside a worker seam that needs redesign.
>
> The minimal design is viable: keep the caller-facing seam near today’s three operations, but hide attempts, worker cursors, relays, operation phases, and user-action custody. The execution must return quickly; request cancellation stops waiting only and does not cancel the durable work. Explicit cancellation becomes a versioned command.
>
> The flexible design reaches the same core conclusion but adds wait sets and child executions. I would not ship that breadth in iteration 1. The strongest direction is a hybrid: minimal `Apply/Read` externally, with today’s retries, reminders, uncertainty, and operation ledger hidden internally—then add new wait kinds only when a real caller requires them.
</details>

Yes. Your proposal is stronger than keeping Tasks out entirely—but only after we deepen it into a reusable durable-execution module. Conversation should become its first real production caller.

The existing Tasks code contains valuable mechanics:

- Idempotent command receipts and optimistic revisions in [TaskNeuron.Commands.cs](./src/Modules/Tasks/Tasks/TaskNeuron.Commands.cs:7).
- Durable redispatch and recovery reminders in [TaskNeuron.Dispatch.cs](./src/Modules/Tasks/Tasks/TaskNeuron.Dispatch.cs:17).
- External-effect tracking through `Prepared → Dispatched → Completed/Uncertain` in [TaskNeuron.Operations.cs](./src/Modules/Tasks/Tasks/TaskNeuron.Operations.cs:26).
- Retry, cancellation, waiting, and user-action concepts.

Orleans reminders survive activation and cluster restarts, although individual missed ticks are not replayed. That makes them suitable as recovery pulses, not as the execution queue itself ([Orleans reminders](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/orleans/grains/timers-and-reminders)).

It cannot be reused unchanged:

- AI worker methods are unimplemented in [GroupChat.cs](./src/Modules/AI/AI/Orchestration/GroupChat.cs:50).
- Worker validation effectively requires the literal `IWorker` grain type, rejecting specialized worker identities in [WorkerDispatchRelayNeuron.cs](./src/Modules/Tasks/Tasks/WorkerDispatchRelayNeuron.cs:55).
- Receipts and operations grow without bounds in [TaskData.cs](./src/Modules/Tasks/Tasks/TaskData.cs:60).
- `OutcomeUncertain` has no resolution path.
- Operation identities include `AttemptId`, so a retry cannot currently suppress the same external side effect across attempts.
- There are no production callers or meaningful failure/restart tests.

### Three interface directions

1. Minimal deep interface:

```csharp
public interface IExecution : INeuron
{
    Task<ExecutionReceipt> Apply(ExecutionCommand command);
    Task<ExecutionSnapshot?> Read();
}
```

Attempts, workers, reminders, cursors, operation phases, and blocker custody become implementation details.

2. Flexible workflow engine:

Adds wait sets, child executions, parallel operations, dependencies, and generic signaling. Powerful, but too broad for stabilization iteration one.

3. Typed caller facade:

```csharp
await runs.StartAsync(
    new ConversationTurn(conversationId, messageId));
```

Excellent for Conversation, but best implemented as an adapter over the minimal core rather than as the durable engine itself.

My recommendation is a hybrid of 1 and 3:

```text
Conversation
    │ typed ConversationTurn adapter
    ▼
Durable Execution: Apply / Read
    │
    └── AI execution adapter
          ├── isolated MAF session
          ├── transient token stream
          ├── durable tool-operation ledger
          └── idempotent final-message append
```

MAF checkpoints and sessions remain internal AI artifacts. They can resume framework workflows, but DigitalBrain still owns execution identity, authorization, storage, and recovery ([MAF checkpoints](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/workflows/checkpoints), [MAF self-hosting](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/hosting/self-hosting/)).

One critical rule: after a non-idempotent MCP operation starts, an unknown outcome must never be automatically retried. It becomes `OutcomeUncertain` until reconciled.

Next decision:

Recommended: **yes**. We can decide its final name—`Tasks` versus `Executions`—next.

Approved: durable execution becomes shared infrastructure, with Conversation as its first production adapter.

The current name `Tasks` is overloaded:

- In C#, `Task` means an asynchronous operation.
- In product language, a Task would naturally mean a user-visible goal or work item.
- What this module actually owns is the durable runtime process of performing work.

Recommended vocabulary:

- **Task** — optional future user-visible goal, such as “research this account.”
- **Execution** — one durable run fulfilling a conversation turn, behavior invocation, or task.
- **Attempt** — one retry generation within an Execution.
- **Operation** — one externally observable effect, such as an MCP tool call.
- **Blocker** — why an Execution is waiting: OAuth, user input, timer, dependency, or uncertain outcome.

Approved and recorded in [CONTEXT.md](./CONTEXT.md): the module owns Executions, while Task is reserved for user-visible work.

Next decision concerns ordering. Two simultaneous turns cannot safely mutate the same Conversation × Responder session.

**Should a Conversation allow exactly one active Execution and queue additional user turns in FIFO order?**

Recommended: **yes**.

- Every submitted message immediately creates a durable queued turn.
- Only the queue head can use the responder session.
- Its responder and history cutoff are frozen when execution starts.
- The UI shows queued/running/failed states.
- Explicit cancellation advances the next queued turn.
- Different Conversations still execute concurrently.

Parallel replies within one Conversation would create nondeterministic transcript ordering, MAF session races, and potentially duplicated tool effects. Multi-agent parallelism can still occur inside the single connected Responder.

> The key distinction is already emerging: MAF Workflows solve orchestration inside a run; our proposed Execution module owns the product-level durable lifecycle around that run. The clean answer is: **MAF Workflows should run inside DigitalBrain Executions, not replace the DigitalBrain Execution abstraction.**

However, Microsoft’s newer **Durable Extension** overlaps heavily with the internals we were planning to build. We should evaluate it before investing deeply in the current Tasks implementation.

## Three different abstractions

| | MAF Workflow / Executor | MAF Durable Extension | DigitalBrain Execution |
|---|---|---|---|
| Primary purpose | Coordinate typed steps inside a run | Durably host and recover MAF runs | Represent a product-owned durable run |
| Best at | Agents, fan-out/fan-in, conditions, shared state, HITL | Recovery, timers, distributed workers, durable waits | Ownership, authorization, commands, cancellation, audit, effects |
| Identity | Workflow/run identity | Durable Task instance/session | Workspace/user/conversation/behavior identity |
| Durability | Checkpoint-resumable, but not a distributed job host by itself | Durable Task-backed distributed execution | Orleans state, reminders, outbox and journals |
| Side effects | Executor responsibility | Steps are checkpointed, but external APIs still need idempotency | Can explicitly track prepared/dispatched/completed/uncertain effects |
| Streaming | Excellent workflow and token events | Reliable streaming needs callbacks and usually a broker such as Redis | Durable final result plus reconnectable UI projection |
| Operational cost | Low | Another scheduler/backend beside Orleans | More custom code, but one existing runtime |

MAF Workflows use typed executors connected by graph edges. They support conditional routing, fan-out/fan-in, request ports and shared state. Their superstep model waits for every active executor in a step before advancing, which is predictable but means one slow branch can block the others. [Microsoft documents that execution model here](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/workflows/workflows).

## What is currently happening in DigitalBrain

DigitalBrain pins MAF Workflows `1.17.0` in [Directory.Packages.props](./Directory.Packages.props:33), but currently uses it only for in-process concurrent/group-chat orchestration in [DirectOrchestrationShape.cs](./src/Modules/AI/AI/Orchestration/DirectOrchestrationShape.cs:73).

We currently do **not** use:

- MAF workflow checkpoints
- A custom checkpoint store
- MAF Durable Task integration
- Durable workflow recovery
- Completed supervised group-chat execution

The MAF agent session is persisted only after the stream completes in [DirectAgentSession.cs](./src/Modules/AI/AI/Orchestration/DirectAgentSession.cs:54). A process failure before that point loses the in-flight progress.

## Pros of using MAF Workflows

- Excellent composition model for explicit, repeatable multi-agent processes.
- Typed messages and graph validation.
- Built-in fan-out, fan-in, conditional routing and human-input requests.
- Executors can encapsulate reusable implementation steps.
- Good streaming and observability events.
- Avoids inventing our own agent graph engine.
- A workflow can be exposed as an agent, keeping Conversation’s responder interface simple.

## Cons of using MAF Workflows as our Execution system

- It does not understand Workspace, User, Conversation, Integration or Surface ownership.
- It does not provide DigitalBrain authorization boundaries.
- Base workflow checkpoints are not the same as accepting and operating a distributed durable job.
- It does not provide our command idempotency, revision conflicts or durable cancellation semantics.
- It cannot guarantee exactly-once Gmail/Salesforce effects.
- Workflow state is framework-specific and introduces migration/versioning concerns.
- Treating every MCP tool as an Executor would recreate the case-specific synapse complexity you dislike.
- Workflow edges would become a second graph model competing with DigitalBrain Connections.

That last point matters: **MAF edges must not become DigitalBrain Connections.** They are private implementation details of a Behavior.

## The Durable Extension changes the calculation

Microsoft now offers `Microsoft.Agents.AI.DurableTask`, which can persist sessions, checkpoint workflows, recover across workers, wait for external events and use Durable Task Scheduler monitoring. It supports both Azure Functions and self-hosted workers. [Microsoft’s Durable Extension documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/integrations/durable-extension) explicitly distinguishes it from ordinary workflow checkpointing.

Its advantages:

- Much less custom scheduling/recovery machinery.
- Durable human/OAuth waits and timers.
- Distributed stateless workers.
- Native durable MAF agents and workflows.
- Operational dashboard and execution history.
- Reliable streaming when configured with a broker.

Its costs:

- The package remains prerelease.
- It introduces Durable Task Scheduler alongside Orleans.
- All agent interactions incur scheduler latency.
- Distributed streaming commonly adds Redis or another broker.
- Durable Task Scheduler agent state has a 1 MB limit; long conversations require manual compaction.
- It still does not own DigitalBrain identity, access, canonical Conversations or external-effect idempotency. [Microsoft lists the current limitations here](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/durable-task/sdks/durable-agents-microsoft-agent-framework).

## Recommended architecture

```text
Conversation
    │
    ▼
DigitalBrain IExecution
(owner, lifecycle, cancellation, blocker, audit)
    │
    ├── simple chat → direct MAF agent loop
    │
    └── approved Behavior → MAF Workflow
                              └── Executors / agents / MCP tools
```

`IExecution` remains a small DigitalBrain-owned contract. Its engine could initially be Orleans-backed and later be replaced by a Durable Extension adapter without exposing MAF types to Conversation or UI.

For example:

- “Summarize my Gmail” → one Execution running a regular tool-using agent. No workflow and no Gmail-specific synapses.
- “Enrich Salesforce accounts weekly using Gmail and web research” → an approved Behavior whose internal implementation may be a MAF Workflow.
- OAuth interruption → a generic Execution blocker resolved by the Integration authorization callback.
- UI disconnect → detaches the observer; it does not cancel the Execution.

My proposed ratification is therefore:

1. Keep `Execution` as the DigitalBrain domain boundary.
2. Use MAF Executors only inside complex Behaviors.
3. Never mirror MAF workflow edges into DigitalBrain Connections.
4. Before deeply refactoring Tasks, run a bounded prove-or-reject comparison between:
   - Orleans-backed Execution
   - MAF Durable Extension-backed Execution
5. Test one conversation turn across restart, OAuth wait/resume, cancellation, reconnect, duplicate submission and uncertain Salesforce write.

This spike should be the next step; otherwise we risk spending months rebuilding functionality Microsoft has just started shipping.

> 201	    }

> 30	            ? synapse

> 41	        try
> 42	        {
> 43	            return await GrainFactory

> 47	        }

> 52	        }

> 55	    private Synapse Adapted(ISynapseTransform transform, Synapse synapse)
> 56	    {
> 57	        try
> 58	        {
> 59	            return transform.Apply(synapse);
> 60	        }
> 61	        catch (Exception failure) when (failure is not NeuronAuthorizationException)
> 62	        {
> 63	            throw new NeuronAuthorizationException(

> 66	        }

> ```csharp
> 1	using DigitalBrain.Abstractions;
> 2	using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;
> 3	
> 4	namespace DigitalBrain.Core;
> 5	
> 6	public abstract partial class Neuron
> 7	{
> 8	    protected Task<SynapseDelivery> SendAsync(NeuronId receiver, Synapse synapse)
> 9	    {
> 10	        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(synapse);
> 11	
> 12	        return FireAsync(synapse, [receiver]);
> 13	    }
> 14	
> 15	    protected Task EmitAsync(Synapse synapse)
> 16	    {
> 17	        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(synapse);
> 18	
> 19	        return EmitAsync(synapse, ResolveEmissionCorrelation());
> 20	    }
> 21	
> 22	    protected CorrelationId ResolveEmissionCorrelation()
> 23	        => _handling?.CorrelationId
> 24	            ?? AmbientClientEntryCorrelation
> 25	            ?? CorrelationId.New();
> 26	
> 27	    protected async Task EmitAsync(Synapse synapse, CorrelationId correlation)
> 28	    {
> 29	        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(synapse);
> 30	
> 31	        var synapseType = synapse.GetType().FullName!;
> 32	        var catalog = ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<BroadcastCatalog>();
> 33	
> 34	        var receivers = catalog.HandlerGrainTypes(synapseType)
> 35	            .Select(grainType => NeuronId.BroadcastReceiver(grainType, Id.Owner, correlation))
> 36	            .Concat(await ConnectedReceiversAsync(synapse).ConfigureAwait(ConfigureAwaitOptions.ContinueOnCapturedContext))
> 37	            .ToArray();
> 38	
> 39	        await FireAsync(synapse, receivers, correlation).ConfigureAwait(ConfigureAwaitOptions.ContinueOnCapturedContext);
> 40	    }
> 41	
> 42	    private async Task<IReadOnlyCollection<NeuronId>> ConnectedReceiversAsync(Synapse synapse)
> 43	    {
> 44	        if (SynapseAlias.Of(synapse.GetType()) is not { } alias)
> 45	        {
> 46	            return [];
> 47	        }
> 48	
> 49	        var graph = ISynapseGraph.ForOwner(Id.Owner);
> 50	        if (graph == Id)
> 51	        {
> 52	            return [];
> 53	        }
> 54	
> 55	        using var bound = new CancellationTokenSource(DeliveryPolicy.ConnectionLookupTimeout);
> 56	        try
> 57	        {
> 58	            var connections = await GrainFactory
> 59	                .GetGrain<ISynapseGraph>(graph.ToGrainId())
> 60	                .ConnectionsFrom(Id, alias)
> 61	                .WaitAsync(bound.Token).ConfigureAwait(true);
> 62	
> 63	            return [.. connections.Select(connection => connection.Transform is null
> 64	                ? connection.Target
> 65	                : ConnectionRelay.ForConnection(Id.Owner, connection.ConnectionId))];
> 66	        }
> 67	        catch (OperationCanceledException) when (bound.IsCancellationRequested)
> 68	        {
> 69	            throw new TimeoutException(
> 70	                $"Synapse graph connection lookup for '{alias}' did not answer within {DeliveryPolicy.ConnectionLookupTimeout}.");
> 71	        }
> 72	    }
> 73	
> 74	    protected async Task EmitAtDepthAsync(Synapse synapse, CorrelationId correlation, int deliveryDepth)
> 75	    {
> 76	        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(synapse);
> 77	
> 78	        ArgumentOutOfRangeException.ThrowIfLessThan(deliveryDepth, 1);
> 79	
> 80	        var restored = CurrentDeliveryDepth;
> 81	        CurrentDeliveryDepth = deliveryDepth - 1;
> 82	        try
> 83	        {
> 84	            await EmitAsync(synapse, correlation).ConfigureAwait(ConfigureAwaitOptions.ContinueOnCapturedContext);
> 85	        }
> 86	        finally
> 87	        {
> 88	            CurrentDeliveryDepth = restored;
> 89	        }
> 90	    }
> 91	
> 92	    private Task<SynapseDelivery> FireAsync(Synapse synapse, NeuronId[] receivers, CorrelationId? correlation = null)
> 93	        => FireAsync(synapse, receivers, _handling, correlation);
> 94	
> 95	    private async Task<SynapseDelivery> FireAsync(
> 96	        Synapse synapse,
> 97	        NeuronId[] receivers,
> 98	        SynapseDelivery? causation,
> 99	        CorrelationId? correlation = null)
> 100	    {
> 101	        var sequence = _outgoing.NextSequence
> 102	            + (_handling is null ? 0 : _firedWhileHandling.Count);
> 103	        var delivery = SynapseDelivery.Create(Snapshot(synapse), Id, sequence, causation, TimeProvider, correlation);
> 104	
> 105	        if (_handling is null)
> 106	        {
> 107	            _outgoing.Append(delivery);
> 108	        }
> 109	        else
> 110	        {
> 111	            _firedWhileHandling.Add(delivery);
> 112	        }
> 113	
> 114	        if (receivers.Length > 0)
> 115	        {
> 116	            _outbox.Add(_entries.SerializeToArray(new OutboxEntry(delivery, receivers, CurrentDeliveryDepth + 1, Attempts: 0)));
> 117	        }
> 118	
> 119	        if (_handling is null)
> 120	        {
> 121	            await CommitAsync(CancellationToken.None).ConfigureAwait(ConfigureAwaitOptions.ContinueOnCapturedContext);
> 122	            await NotifyWatchersAsync().ConfigureAwait(ConfigureAwaitOptions.ContinueOnCapturedContext);
> 123	            ScheduleDrain();
> 124	        }
> 125	
> 126	        return delivery;
> 127	    }
> 128	}

> 211	    private async Task<string> SendAsync(
> 212	        Synapse request,
> 213	        Type requestType,
> 214	        NeuronId target,
> 215	        CancellationToken cancellationToken)
> 216	    {
> 217	        var sessionId = ISessionNeuron.ForOwner(owner);
> 218	        var session = grains.GetGrain<ISessionNeuron>(sessionId.ToGrainId());
> 219	
> 220	        var responseType = ReplyTypeOf(requestType);
> 221	        var opened = await session
> 222	            .ReadNeuronJournal(sessionId, JournalKind.Incoming, long.MaxValue)
> 223	            .ConfigureAwait(false);
> 224	        var cursor = opened.ResumeSequence;
> 225	        var delivery = await session.Fire(target, request).ConfigureAwait(false);
> 226	
> 227	        if (responseType is null)
> 228	        {
> 229	            return $"Delivered to {target}.";
> 230	        }
> 231	
> 232	        var abandonAfter = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow + ReplyWait;
> 233	        while (true)
> 234	        {
> 235	            var read = await session
> 236	                .ReadNeuronJournal(sessionId, JournalKind.Incoming, cursor)
> 237	                .ConfigureAwait(false);
> 238	
> 239	            foreach (var journaled in read.Delta)
> 240	            {
> 241	                if (journaled.CorrelationId == delivery.CorrelationId
> 242	                    && responseType.IsInstanceOfType(journaled.Synapse))
> 243	                {
> 244	                    return JsonSerializer.Serialize(journaled.Synapse, responseType);
> 245	                }
> 246	            }
> 247	
> 248	            cursor = read.ResumeSequence;
> 249	
> 250	            if (DateTimeOffset.UtcNow >= abandonAfter)
> 251	            {
> 252	                return $"No {responseType.Name} reply from {target} within "
> 253	                    + $"{ReplyWait.TotalSeconds:F0}s. The request is "
> 254	                    + "committed; the target may be unconfigured or refusing — tell the owner what "
> 255	                    + "you attempted rather than claiming it worked.";
> 256	            }
> 257	
> 258	            await Task.Delay(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(25), cancellationToken).ConfigureAwait(false);
> 259	        }
> 260	    }
> 261	
> 262	    // A named instance of a type that has live instances — but is none of them and
> 263	    // not the default — is almost always a guessed identity (the timer:dev/timer bug).

> 158	        }

> 160	        if (pending.ParkRevision != expectedParkRevision)
> 161	        {
> 162	            throw new NeuronAuthorizationException(
> 163	                $"Task '{Id}' is parked at revision {pending.ParkRevision}, not expected park revision {expectedParkRevision}.");
> 164	        }
> 165	
> 166	        if (pending.ActionEpoch != actionEpoch)
> 167	        {
> 168	            throw new NeuronAuthorizationException(
> 169	                $"Task '{Id}' rejected an action epoch that does not match the parked user action.");
> 170	        }
> 171	
> 172	        if (pending.ActionReference != actionReference)
> 173	        {
> 174	            throw new NeuronAuthorizationException(
> 175	                $"Task '{Id}' rejected an action reference that does not match the parked user action.");
> 176	        }
> 177	
> 178	        if (pending.ExpiresAt <= TimeProvider.GetUtcNow())
> 179	        {
> 180	            throw new NeuronAuthorizationException(
> 181	                $"Task '{Id}' rejected an expired user-action reference.");
> 182	        }
> 183	
> 184	        return pending;
> 185	    }
> 186	
> 187	    private Task<SynapseDelivery> SendParkReadyAsync(UserActionRequired control)

> 129	        data.Result = null;
> 130	        data.Failure = new UserActionDenied(pending.ModuleId);
> 131	        data.Evidence = [];
> 132	        data.PendingDispatch = null;
> 133	
> 134	        var snapshot = Snapshot(data);
> 135	        data.Receipts.Add(command.CommandId, snapshot);
> 136	
> 137	        StageForTurn(data);
> 138	        await UnregisterReminderAsync(RetryReminderName).ConfigureAwait(ConfigureAwaitOptions.ContinueOnCapturedContext);
> 139	        await UnregisterReminderAsync(DispatchReminderName).ConfigureAwait(ConfigureAwaitOptions.ContinueOnCapturedContext);
> 140	    }
> 141	
> 142	    private UserActionPending RequireUserActionAuthority(
> 143	        TaskData data,
> 144	        ProtectedPayloadReference actionReference,
> 145	        Guid actionEpoch,
> 146	        long expectedParkRevision)
> 147	    {
> 148	        if (data.State != TaskState.Waiting || data.Blocker is not UserActionPending pending)
> 149	        {
> 150	            throw new NeuronAuthorizationException(
> 151	                $"Task '{Id}' is not waiting on a module user action.");
> 152	        }
> 153	
> 154	        if (data.ActiveAttempt is null)
> 155	        {
> 156	            throw new NeuronAuthorizationException(
> 157	                $"Task '{Id}' has no active attempt bound to the user action.");
> 158	        }
> 159	
> 160	        if (pending.ParkRevision != expectedParkRevision)
> 161	        {
> 162	            throw new NeuronAuthorizationException(
> 163	                $"Task '{Id}' is parked at revision {pending.ParkRevision}, not expected park revision {expectedParkRevision}.");
> 164	        }
> 165	
> 166	        if (pending.ActionEpoch != actionEpoch)
> 167	        {
> 168	            throw new NeuronAuthorizationException(
> 169	                $"Task '{Id}' rejected an action epoch that does not match the parked user action.");
> 170	        }
> 171	
> 172	        if (pending.ActionReference != actionReference)
> 173	        {
> 174	            throw new NeuronAuthorizationException(
> 175	                $"Task '{Id}' rejected an action reference that does not match the parked user action.");
> 176	        }
> 177	
> 178	        if (pending.ExpiresAt <= TimeProvider.GetUtcNow())
> 179	        {
> 180	            throw new NeuronAuthorizationException(
> 181	                $"Task '{Id}' rejected an expired user-action reference.");
> 182	        }
> 183	
> 184	        return pending;
> 185	    }
> 186	
> 187	    private Task<SynapseDelivery> SendParkReadyAsync(UserActionRequired control)
> 188	        => SendAsync(
> 189	            control.Completer,
> 190	            new UserActionParkReady(

> 193	                control.Module,

> 195	                control.ActionReference,

> 114	        if (!TryParseReminderName(reminderName, out var generation))

> 121	    }
> 122	
> 123	    private async Task ElapseIfDue(long generation, string reminderName)
> 124	    {
> 125	        var data = LoadRecorded();
> 126	
> 127	        if (data is null
> 128	            || data.Status != TimerStatus.Scheduled
> 129	            || data.Generation != generation
> 130	            || !string.Equals(data.ActiveReminderName, reminderName, StringComparison.Ordinal))
> 131	        {
> 132	            await RetireReminderAsync(reminderName).ConfigureAwait(ConfigureAwaitOptions.ContinueOnCapturedContext);
> 133	            return;
> 134	        }
> 135	
> 136	        var observedAt = TimeProvider.GetUtcNow();
> 137	        if (observedAt < data.DueAt)
> 138	        {
> 139	            await RegisterReminderAsync(reminderName, data.DueAt - observedAt).ConfigureAwait(ConfigureAwaitOptions.ContinueOnCapturedContext);
> 140	            return;
> 141	        }
> 142	
> 143	        var resolution = observedAt > data.DueAt + ReminderPeriod
> 144	            ? TimerResolution.Recovered
> 145	            : TimerResolution.OnTime;
> 146	        var rollbackState = SerializedState();
> 147	        Stage(data with { Status = TimerStatus.Elapsed, ActiveReminderName = null });
> 148	
> 149	        try
> 150	        {
> 151	            await EmitAsync(new TimerElapsed(
> 152	                Id,
> 153	                generation,
> 154	                data.ScheduledAt,
> 155	                data.DueAt,
> 156	                observedAt,
> 157	                resolution,
> 158	                data.Note)).ConfigureAwait(ConfigureAwaitOptions.ContinueOnCapturedContext);
> 159	        }
> 160	        catch
> 161	        {
> 162	            RestoreState(rollbackState);
> 163	            DeactivateOnIdle();
> 164	            throw;
> 165	        }
> 166	
> 167	        await RetireReminderAsync(reminderName).ConfigureAwait(ConfigureAwaitOptions.ContinueOnCapturedContext);
> 168	    }
> 169	
> 170	    private TimerState? LoadRecorded()
> 171	        => _state.Value is { Length: > 0 } serialized
> 172	            ? _states.Deserialize(serialized)
> 173	            : null;

> 206	      }
> 207	    } finally {
> 208	      _aborts.remove(abort);
> 209	    }
> 210	  }
> 211	
> 212	  Future<void> cancelInflight() async {
> 213	    for (final abort in List<Completer<void>>.of(_aborts)) {
> 214	      if (!abort.isCompleted) {
> 215	        abort.complete();
> 216	      }
> 217	    }
> 218	    _aborts.clear();
> 219	  }
> 220	
> 221	  void close() {
> 222	    unawaited(cancelInflight());
> 223	    if (_ownsClient) {
> 224	      _http.close();
> 225	    }
> 226	  }

> 272	        );
> 273	      }
> 274	      if (response.body.isEmpty) {

> 278	    } finally {
> 279	      _aborts.remove(abort);

> 18	
> 19	    private DirectOrchestrationShape(
> 20	        Type orchestrationType,
> 21	        IReadOnlyList<Participant> participants,
> 22	        DirectOrchestrationIdentity identity,
> 23	        Func<AIAgent[], Workflow> buildWorkflow,
> 24	        IWorkflowExecutionEnvironment executionEnvironment)
> 25	    {
> 26	        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(orchestrationType);
> 27	        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(participants);
> 28	        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(identity);

> 33	        _buildWorkflow = buildWorkflow;
> 34	        _executionEnvironment = executionEnvironment;
> 35	        Invocations = new([.. participants.Select(participant => participant.Id)]);
> 36	        Definition = OrchestrationDefinition.Describe(orchestrationType, participants, identity);
> 37	    }
> 38	
> 39	    internal OrchestrationDefinition Definition { get; }
> 40	
> 41	    internal ParticipantInvocations Invocations { get; }
> 42	
> 43	    internal static Participant[] Snapshot(NeuronId orchestration, IReadOnlyList<Participant>? participants)
> 44	    {
> 45	        if (participants is null)
> 46	        {
> 47	            throw new InvalidOperationException("Participants returned null.");
> 48	        }
> 49	
> 50	        var snapshot = participants.ToArray();
> 51	
> 52	        if (snapshot.Length == 0)
> 53	        {
> 54	            throw new InvalidOperationException(
> 55	                $"AI orchestration '{orchestration}' requires at least one participant.");
> 56	        }
> 57	
> 58	        if (snapshot.Any(participant => participant is null))
> 59	        {
> 60	            throw new InvalidOperationException(
> 61	                $"AI orchestration '{orchestration}' has a null participant.");
> 62	        }
> 63	
> 64	        if (snapshot.Any(participant => participant.Id.Owner != orchestration.Owner))
> 65	        {
> 66	            throw new InvalidOperationException(
> 67	                $"Every participant in AI orchestration '{orchestration}' must belong to its owner.");
> 68	        }
> 69	
> 70	        return snapshot;
> 71	    }
> 72	
> 73	    internal static DirectOrchestrationShape CreateConcurrent(Type orchestrationType, IReadOnlyList<Participant> participants)
> 74	        => new(
> 75	            orchestrationType,
> 76	            participants,
> 77	            new("concurrent", "in-process-concurrent", "concurrent-default", static _ => "none"),
> 78	            static agents => AgentWorkflowBuilder.BuildConcurrent(agents),
> 79	            InProcessExecution.Concurrent);
> 80	
> 81	    internal static DirectOrchestrationShape CreateGroupChat(Type orchestrationType, IReadOnlyList<Participant> participants)
> 82	        => new(
> 83	            orchestrationType,
> 84	            participants,
> 85	            new("group-chat", "in-process-lockstep", "none", static count => $"round-robin:{count}"),
> 86	            static agents => AgentWorkflowBuilder
> 87	                .CreateGroupChatBuilderWith(team => new RoundRobinGroupChatManager(team)
> 88	                {
> 89	                    MaximumIterationCount = agents.Length,
> 90	                })
> 91	                .AddParticipants(agents)
> 92	                .Build(),
> 93	            InProcessExecution.Lockstep);
> 94	
> 95	    internal AIAgent CreateAgent(IGrainFactory grains, TaskScheduler turnScheduler)
> 96	    {
> 97	        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(grains);
> 98	        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(turnScheduler);
> 99	
> 100	        AIAgent[] agents =
> 101	        [
> 102	            .. _participants.Select(participant => participant.CreateAgent(grains, turnScheduler, Invocations)),
> 103	        ];
> 104	
> 105	        return _buildWorkflow(agents).AsAIAgent(id: Definition.HostId, executionEnvironment: _executionEnvironment);
> 106	    }
> 107	}

> **`src/Kernel/Aspire/DigitalBrain.Aspire/DigitalBrainRuntimeHostingExtensions.cs`** — AddDigitalBrain(method)

> ```csharp
> 1	using DigitalBrain.Abstractions;
> 2	using DigitalBrain.Core;
> 3	using DigitalBrain.ServiceDefaults;
> 4	using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;
> 5	using Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting;
> 6	using Orleans.Configuration;
> 7	using Orleans.Dashboard;
> 8	
> 9	namespace DigitalBrain.Aspire;
> 10	
> 11	public static class DigitalBrainRuntimeHostingExtensions
> 12	{
> 13	    // Deliberate Azure Queue stream layout for a small single-silo product composition:
> 14	    // ~8 physical queues, ~20 streams/queue headroom (2× safety). Visibility is double a
> 15	    // one-minute cache window. Azure Queue streams are at-least-once, not rewindable, and
> 16	    // not FIFO under failure — weaker than the durable synapse outbox; do not move outbox
> 17	    // traffic onto this provider.
> 18	    internal const int StreamQueueCount = 8;
> 19	    internal static readonly TimeSpan StreamMessageVisibilityTimeout = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(2);
> 20	
> 21	    public static IHostApplicationBuilder AddDigitalBrain(
> 22	        this IHostApplicationBuilder builder,
> 23	        ModuleAssemblies modules)
> 24	    {
> 25	        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(builder);
> 26	        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(modules);
> 27	
> 28	        builder.AddServiceDefaults();
> 29	        builder.AddKeyedAzureTableServiceClient(DigitalBrainResourceNames.Clustering);
> 30	        builder.AddKeyedAzureTableServiceClient(DigitalBrainResourceNames.Reminders);
> 31	        builder.AddKeyedAzureQueueServiceClient(DigitalBrainResourceNames.Streams);
> 32	        builder.AddKeyedAzureTableServiceClient(DigitalBrainResourceNames.PubSub);
> 33	        builder.UseOrleans(silo =>
> 34	        {
> 35	            silo.AddDigitalBrainJournalStorage(builder.Configuration);
> 36	            DigitalBrainRuntime.Add(silo, modules);
> 37	            silo.Services
> 38	                .AddOptions<HashRingStreamQueueMapperOptions>(DigitalBrainResourceNames.StreamProviderName)
> 39	                .Configure(options => options.TotalQueueCount = StreamQueueCount);
> 40	            silo.Services
> 41	                .AddOptions<AzureQueueOptions>(DigitalBrainResourceNames.StreamProviderName)
> 42	                .Configure(options => options.MessageVisibilityTimeout = StreamMessageVisibilityTimeout);
> 43	            silo.AddDashboard(options =>
> 44	            {
> 45	                options.CounterUpdateIntervalMs = 5000;
> 46	                options.HistoryLength = 200;
> 47	            });
> 48	        });
> 49	        builder.AddDigitalBrainOwner(activateOnStart: false);
> 50	        return builder;
> 51	    }
> 52	}

> 35	            services.GetRequiredService<IDurablePayloadProtector>(),
> 36	            commit,
> 37	            neuron);
> 38	    }
> 39	
> 40	    internal bool HasDurableSession => state.Value is { Length: > 0 };
> 41	
> 42	    internal async IAsyncEnumerable<ChatResponseUpdate> RunStreamingAsync(
> 43	        AIAgent agent,
> 44	        OrchestrationDefinition definition,
> 45	        ParticipantInvocations invocations,

> 52	        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(messages);

> 54	        var session = state.Value is { Length: > 0 } serialized

> 56	            : await agent.CreateSessionAsync(cancellationToken).ConfigureAwait(false);
> 57	
> 58	        await foreach (var update in agent.RunStreamingAsync(messages, session, cancellationToken: cancellationToken).ConfigureAwait(false))
> 59	        {
> 60	            cancellationToken.ThrowIfCancellationRequested();
> 61	
> 62	            yield return update.AsChatResponseUpdate();
> 63	        }
> 64	
> 65	        cancellationToken.ThrowIfCancellationRequested();
> 66	
> 67	        invocations.RequireAnyInvoked(neuron);
> 68	
> 69	        await PersistSessionAsync(agent, session, definition, cancellationToken).ConfigureAwait(false);
> 70	    }
> 71	
> 72	    private async Task PersistSessionAsync(
> 73	        AIAgent agent,
> 74	        AgentSession session,
> 75	        OrchestrationDefinition definition,
> 76	        CancellationToken cancellationToken)
> 77	    {
> 78	        var serializedSession = await agent.SerializeSessionAsync(session, cancellationToken: cancellationToken).ConfigureAwait(false);
> 79	        var protectedSession = protector.Protect(
> 80	            Purpose(definition.Fingerprint),
> 81	            Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(serializedSession.GetRawText()));
> 82	        var envelope = new DirectAgentSessionEnvelope(CurrentEnvelopeVersion, definition, protectedSession);
> 83	        var previous = state.Value?.ToArray();
> 84	
> 85	        state.Value = JsonSerializer.SerializeToUtf8Bytes(envelope);
> 86	
> 87	        try
> 88	        {
> 89	            await commit().ConfigureAwait(false);
> 90	        }
> 91	        catch
> 92	        {
> 93	            state.Value = previous;
> 94	            throw;
> 95	        }
> 96	    }

> 99	        AIAgent agent,
> 100	        byte[] serialized,
> 101	        OrchestrationDefinition definition,
> 102	        CancellationToken cancellationToken)
> 103	    {
> 104	        DirectAgentSessionEnvelope stored;
> 105	
> 106	        try
> 107	        {
> 108	            stored = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<DirectAgentSessionEnvelope>(serialized)
> 109	                ?? throw RecoveryRequired();
> 110	        }
> 111	        catch (Exception failure) when (failure is JsonException or NotSupportedException)
> 112	        {
> 113	            throw RecoveryRequired(failure);
> 114	        }
> 115	
> 116	        if (stored.EnvelopeVersion != CurrentEnvelopeVersion
> 117	            || stored.Definition is null
> 118	            || stored.ProtectedSession is null)
> 119	        {
> 120	            throw RecoveryRequired();
> 121	        }
> 122	
> 123	        if (!string.Equals(stored.Definition.Fingerprint, definition.Fingerprint, StringComparison.Ordinal))
> 124	        {
> 125	            throw new InvalidOperationException(
> 126	                "The durable direct-agent session is incompatible with the current orchestration definition; an explicit migration or reset is required.");
> 127	        }
> 128	
> 129	        try
> 130	        {
> 131	            var sessionBytes = protector.Unprotect(Purpose(definition.Fingerprint), stored.ProtectedSession);
> 132	            using var sessionJson = JsonDocument.Parse(sessionBytes);
> 133	
> 134	            return await agent.DeserializeSessionAsync(
> 135	                sessionJson.RootElement.Clone(),
> 136	                cancellationToken: cancellationToken).ConfigureAwait(false);
> 137	        }
> 138	        catch (Exception failure) when (failure is CryptographicException
> 139	            or JsonException
> 140	            or FormatException
> 141	            or InvalidOperationException
> 142	            or NotSupportedException)
> 143	        {
> 144	            throw RecoveryRequired(failure);
> 145	        }
> 146	    }

> **`src/Kernel/DigitalBrain.Core/Capabilities/ModuleReflection.cs`** — ManifestOf(method), ModuleReflection(class), Humanized(method), NeuronContracts(method), FactVocabulary(method), ContractsSuffix(constant), +10 more
>
> ```csharp
> 1	using System.Reflection;
> 2	using System.Text;
> 3	using DigitalBrain.Abstractions;
> 4	
> 5	namespace DigitalBrain.Core;
> 6	
> 7	public static class ModuleReflection
> 8	{
> 9	    private const string ContractsSuffix = ".Contracts";
> 10	    private const string DefaultInstanceMemberName = "DefaultInstanceName";
> 11	
> 12	    public static CapabilityManifest ManifestOf(Assembly contracts)
> 13	    {
> 14	        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(contracts);
> 15	
> 16	        var assemblyName = contracts.GetName().Name
> 17	            ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("A contracts assembly must carry a name.");
> 18	        var moduleName = assemblyName.EndsWith(ContractsSuffix, StringComparison.Ordinal)
> 19	            ? assemblyName[..^ContractsSuffix.Length]
> 20	            : assemblyName;
> 21	
> 22	        return new CapabilityManifest(
> 23	            new ModuleId(moduleName),
> 24	            "1.0.0",
> 25	            Humanized(moduleName[(moduleName.LastIndexOf('.') + 1)..]),
> 26	            [.. NeuronContracts(contracts).Select(Described)],
> 27	            [.. FactVocabulary(contracts)]);
> 28	    }
> 29	
> 30	    private static IEnumerable<Type> NeuronContracts(Assembly contracts)
> 31	        => SafeTypes(contracts)
> 32	            .Where(static type => type is { IsInterface: true, IsPublic: true }
> 33	                && type != typeof(INeuron)
> 34	                && typeof(INeuron).IsAssignableFrom(type))
> 35	            .OrderBy(static type => type.Name, StringComparer.Ordinal);
> 36	
> 37	    private static NeuronCapabilityDescriptor Described(Type neuronContract)
> 38	    {
> 39	        var accepted = HandledSynapses(neuronContract)
> 40	            .Select(DescriptorFor)
> 41	            .ToArray();
> 42	        var emitted = HandledSynapses(neuronContract)
> 43	            .Select(ReplyTypeOf)
> 44	            .OfType<Type>()
> 45	            .Distinct()
> 46	            .Select(DescriptorFor)
> 47	            .ToArray();
> 48	
> 49	        return new NeuronCapabilityDescriptor(
> 50	            ContractIdOf(neuronContract),
> 51	            Humanized(TrimmedInterfaceName(neuronContract)),
> 52	            DefaultInstanceNameOf(neuronContract),
> 53	            accepted,
> 54	            emitted);
> 55	    }
> 56	
> 57	    private static IEnumerable<Type> HandledSynapses(Type neuronContract)
> 58	        => neuronContract.GetInterfaces()
> 59	            .Where(static contract => contract.IsGenericType
> 60	                && contract.GetGenericTypeDefinition() == typeof(IHandle<>))
> 61	            .Select(static contract => contract.GenericTypeArguments[0])
> 62	            .OrderBy(static synapse => synapse.Name, StringComparer.Ordinal);
> 63	
> 64	    private static IEnumerable<SynapseCapabilityDescriptor> FactVocabulary(Assembly contracts)
> 65	        => SafeTypes(contracts)
> 66	            .Where(static type => type is { IsClass: true, IsAbstract: false }
> 67	                && typeof(Synapse).IsAssignableFrom(type))
> 68	            .OrderBy(static type => type.Name, StringComparer.Ordinal)
> 69	            .Select(DescriptorFor);
> 70	
> 71	    private static IEnumerable<Type> SafeTypes(Assembly assembly)
> 72	    {
> 73	        try
> 74	        {
> 75	            return assembly.GetTypes();
> 76	        }
> 77	        catch (ReflectionTypeLoadException partiallyLoaded)
> 78	        {
> 79	            return partiallyLoaded.Types.OfType<Type>();
> 80	        }
> 81	    }
> 82	
> 83	    private static SynapseCapabilityDescriptor DescriptorFor(Type synapse)
> 84	        => new(
> 85	            SynapseAlias.Of(synapse) ?? synapse.Name,
> 86	            1,
> 87	            Humanized(synapse.Name),
> 88	            CapabilitySchema.For(synapse));
> 89	
> 90	    private static Type? ReplyTypeOf(Type synapse)
> 91	    {
> 92	        for (var probed = synapse.BaseType; probed is not null; probed = probed.BaseType)
> 93	        {
> 94	            if (probed.IsGenericType && probed.GetGenericTypeDefinition() == typeof(RequestSynapse<>))
> 95	            {
> 96	                return probed.GenericTypeArguments[0];
> 97	            }
> 98	        }
> 99	
> 100	        return null;
> 101	    }
> 102	
> 103	    private static string ContractIdOf(Type neuronContract)
> 104	        => neuronContract.GetCustomAttributesData()
> 105	                .FirstOrDefault(static attribute => attribute.AttributeType == typeof(AliasAttribute))?
> 106	                .ConstructorArguments[0].Value as string
> 107	            ?? TrimmedInterfaceName(neuronContract).ToLowerInvariant();
> 108	
> 109	    private static string DefaultInstanceNameOf(Type neuronContract)
> 110	        => neuronContract.GetField(DefaultInstanceMemberName)?.GetRawConstantValue() as string
> 111	            ?? neuronContract.GetField("InstanceName")?.GetRawConstantValue() as string
> 112	            ?? "default";
> 113	
> 114	    private static string TrimmedInterfaceName(Type contract)
> 115	        => contract.Name.Length > 1 && contract.Name[0] == 'I' && char.IsUpper(contract.Name[1])
> 116	            ? contract.Name[1..]
> 117	            : contract.Name;
> 118	
> 119	    // "StartTimer" → "Start timer"; "time.start-timer" callers pass type names, not aliases.
> 120	    private static string Humanized(string identifier)
> 121	    {
> 122	        var words = new StringBuilder(identifier.Length + 8);
> 123	
> 124	        for (var index = 0; index < identifier.Length; index++)
> 125	        {
> 126	            var letter = identifier[index];
> 127	            if (index > 0 && char.IsUpper(letter) && !char.IsUpper(identifier[index - 1]))
> 128	            {
> 129	                words.Append(' ').Append(char.ToLowerInvariant(letter));
> 130	                continue;
> 131	            }
> 132	
> 133	            words.Append(letter);
> 134	        }
> 135	
> 136	        return words.ToString();
> 137	    }
> 138	}

> **`src/Kernel/DigitalBrain.Core/Capabilities/ActiveCapabilityCatalog.cs`** — ActiveCapabilityCatalog(method), Create(method), TryGetModule(method), _modules(field), Modules(property)

> ```csharp
> 1	using DigitalBrain.Abstractions;
> 2	
> 3	namespace DigitalBrain.Core;
> 4	
> 5	public sealed class ActiveCapabilityCatalog
> 6	{
> 7	    private readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<string, CapabilityManifest> _modules;
> 8	    private readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<string, NeuronCapabilityDescriptor> _neurons;
> 9	    private readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<(string ContractId, int SchemaVersion), SynapseCapabilityDescriptor> _synapses;
> 10	
> 11	    private ActiveCapabilityCatalog(
> 12	        IReadOnlyList<CapabilityManifest> modules,
> 13	        IReadOnlyDictionary<string, CapabilityManifest> moduleIndex,
> 14	        IReadOnlyDictionary<string, NeuronCapabilityDescriptor> neurons,
> 15	        IReadOnlyDictionary<(string ContractId, int SchemaVersion), SynapseCapabilityDescriptor> synapses)
> 16	    {
> 17	        Modules = modules;
> 18	        _modules = moduleIndex;
> 19	        _neurons = neurons;
> 20	        _synapses = synapses;
> 21	    }
> 22	
> 23	    public IReadOnlyList<CapabilityManifest> Modules { get; }
> 24	
> 25	    public static ActiveCapabilityCatalog Create(IReadOnlyList<CapabilityManifest> manifests)
> 26	    {
> 27	        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(manifests);
> 28	
> 29	        CapabilityManifest[] ordered =
> 30	        [
> 31	            .. manifests.OrderBy(static manifest => manifest.ModuleId.Value, StringComparer.Ordinal),
> 32	        ];
> 33	
> 34	        var moduleIndex = new Dictionary<string, CapabilityManifest>(StringComparer.Ordinal);
> 35	        var neurons = new Dictionary<string, NeuronCapabilityDescriptor>(StringComparer.Ordinal);
> 36	        var neuronOwners = new Dictionary<string, ModuleId>(StringComparer.Ordinal);
> 37	        var synapses = new Dictionary<(string, int), SynapseCapabilityDescriptor>();
> 38	
> 39	        foreach (var manifest in ordered)
> 40	        {
> 41	            if (!moduleIndex.TryAdd(manifest.ModuleId.Value, manifest))
> 42	            {
> 43	                throw new InvalidOperationException(
> 44	                    $"Duplicate active module capability id '{manifest.ModuleId.Value}'.");
> 45	            }
> 46	
> 47	            foreach (var neuron in manifest.Neurons)
> 48	            {
> 49	                if (!neurons.TryAdd(neuron.ContractId, neuron))
> 50	                {
> 51	                    var prior = neuronOwners[neuron.ContractId];
> 52	                    throw new InvalidOperationException(
> 53	                        $"Duplicate active neuron capability id '{neuron.ContractId}' "
> 54	                        + $"from modules '{prior.Value}' and '{manifest.ModuleId.Value}'.");
> 55	                }
> 56	
> 57	                neuronOwners[neuron.ContractId] = manifest.ModuleId;
> 58	                IndexSynapses(synapses, neuron.Accepted, neuron.ContractId);
> 59	                IndexSynapses(synapses, neuron.Emitted, neuron.ContractId);
> 60	            }
> 61	        }
> 62

> 81	    private static void IndexSynapses(
> 82	        Dictionary<(string, int), SynapseCapabilityDescriptor> synapses,
> 83	        IReadOnlyList<SynapseCapabilityDescriptor> descriptors,
> 84	        string neuronContractId)
> 85	    {
> 86	        foreach (var synapse in descriptors)
> 87	        {
> 88	            var key = (synapse.ContractId, synapse.SchemaVersion);
> 89	            if (synapses.TryGetValue(key, out var existing)
> 90	                && !string.Equals(existing.JsonSchema, synapse.JsonSchema, StringComparison.Ordinal))
> 91	            {
> 92	                throw new InvalidOperationException(
> 93	                    $"Incompatible active schemas for synapse '{synapse.ContractId}' v{synapse.SchemaVersion} "
> 94	                    + $"(seen via neuron '{neuronContractId}').");
> 95	            }
> 96	
> 97	            if (!synapses.TryAdd(key, synapse)
> 98	                && !string.Equals(synapses[key].JsonSchema, synapse.JsonSchema, StringComparison.Ordinal))
> 99	            {
> 100	                throw new InvalidOperationException(
> 101	                    $"Duplicate incompatible synapse capability '{synapse.ContractId}' v{synapse.SchemaVersion}.");
> 102	            }
> 103	        }
> 104	    }

> 56	                        neuron.GrainKey,
> 57	                        placements[neuron.Silo]))
> 58	                    .OrderBy(static neuron => neuron.GrainType, StringComparer.Ordinal)

> The code comparison is sharper than a simple “ours versus theirs”: DigitalBrain currently has a durable, owner-scoped event-topology graph, while MAF has a typed control-flow graph for one workflow run. They look alike visually but solve different problems. The danger is turning DigitalBrain Connections into workflow edges; that would give us two weaker copies of MAF rather than a product advantage.

You are half-right.

**MAF Durable Extension is no longer Azure Functions-only**, but **Orleans cannot replace its durable execution engine through a supported adapter**.

Microsoft now supports:

- Azure Functions hosting.
- Self-hosted/BYOC workers in a container, service, Kubernetes, or another .NET host.

But the self-hosted version still runs a Durable Task worker connected to a Durable Task backend—normally Durable Task Scheduler. Hosting it beside an Orleans silo does not make Orleans its scheduler. [Microsoft documents both hosting modes here](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/integrations/durable-extension).

There is no official Orleans Durable Task provider. Building one would mean implementing history replay, leases, timers, entities, external events and work dispatch—in effect, rebuilding Durable Task.

What Orleans can do is implement MAF’s ordinary [`ICheckpointStore<T>`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.agents.ai.workflows.checkpointing.icheckpointstore-1?view=agent-framework-dotnet-latest). That gives an in-process MAF Workflow Orleans-backed checkpoints. It does **not** turn Orleans into the MAF Durable runtime.

So:

```text
MAF Durable Extension + Orleans
= two distributed runtimes

MAF Workflow + Orleans Execution + Orleans checkpoint adapter
= one distributed runtime, with MAF used as an inner workflow engine
```

For our current scale and stabilize-first goal, I recommend the second.

## The graphs are not equivalent

“Graph” is currently overloaded. There are at least three distinct things:

| Graph | Meaning | Lifetime |
|---|---|---|
| DigitalBrain Connection graph | Durable relationships and fact routing between addressable Neurons | Long-lived and mutable |
| MAF Workflow graph | Typed control flow between Executors for one bounded Behavior | Definition/run scoped |
| Flutter topology graph | Read-only visualization of Modules, Neurons and Connections | UI projection |

DigitalBrain’s [SynapseGraphNeuron.cs](./src/Kernel/DigitalBrain.Core/Neuron/SynapseGraphNeuron.cs:9) stores owner-scoped Connections. When a Neuron emits a fact, [Neuron.Messaging.cs](./src/Kernel/DigitalBrain.Core/Neuron/Neuron.Messaging.cs:27) resolves matching Connections and places deliveries in its durable outbox.

MAF’s Workflow graph instead provides start/output/completion, typed routing, conditions, fan-out/fan-in, joins, workflow-local state and checkpoints. It uses synchronized supersteps and waits for all active Executors before advancing. [That execution model is documented here](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/workflows/workflows).

Superficially both have nodes and edges. Semantically:

```text
Connection:
“When this durable brain part emits this fact, deliver it there.”

Workflow edge:
“After this bounded step produces this type, execute that step.”
```

Trying to make Connections also represent workflow steps would weaken our architecture. We would have no clear completion, joins, workflow-local state, atomic workflow revisions or deterministic resumption.

## Modules and Executors are also different

A comparison between a DigitalBrain Module and a MAF Executor is a category error:

- A **Module** supplies a coherent capability: AI, Gmail, Salesforce, Conversation, Surface, Execution.
- A **Neuron** is an addressable, potentially durable runtime entity.
- An **Executor** is one processing step inside a Workflow.
- A **Behavior** is the closest DigitalBrain counterpart to a MAF Workflow.
- An **Execution** is the closest counterpart to a MAF Run, but with product identity, authorization and effect semantics.
- MAF has no counterpart for a shared Surface, Workspace publication or Integration ownership.

A generated Salesforce enrichment should therefore be a **Behavior revision**, not a new Module and not a collection of new Salesforce-specific Connections.

## Are we better?

The honest verdict is:

> DigitalBrain has a more ambitious and potentially better product architecture, but today it is not a more complete product or a better workflow engine.

### Where DigitalBrain is genuinely stronger

- Durable, owner-scoped Neuron identities.
- Runtime wiring of already-installed capabilities.
- Journals, causation/correlation and durable outbox delivery.
- Product concepts MAF intentionally does not provide: Workspace, Integration, Conversation, Surface, sharing and publication.
- Introspection across Modules, Neurons, Connections and activity.
- One model-facing capability interface: discover capabilities, resolve Neurons and fire typed Synapses.

The Neuron messaging Module is genuinely deep: a caller uses `EmitAsync`, while journaling, correlation, durable delivery and retries remain hidden inside.

### Where MAF is substantially stronger

- Typed and validated workflow edges.
- Conditional execution, fan-out/fan-in and joins.
- Clear run start, halt, result and completion.
- Workflow-local and shared state.
- Checkpoint/resume and request/response ports.
- Workflow events and execution visualization.
- Established multi-agent orchestration patterns.

DigitalBrain currently delegates concurrent and group-chat execution to MAF’s in-process implementation in [DirectOrchestrationShape.cs](./src/Modules/AI/AI/Orchestration/DirectOrchestrationShape.cs:73). We are not currently using general custom Executors or workflow checkpoints.

### Where DigitalBrain is currently still a demo

- [Surface.cs](./src/Modules/UI/DigitalBrain.Modules.UI/Surface/Surface.cs:9) only emits `SurfaceOpened`; `ControlActivated` does nothing. There is no durable layout, component tree, chart binding or sharing state.
- Behavior Studio explicitly reports that the Behavior host is not in the product composition and falls back to demo fixtures in [behavior_view_model.dart](./src/Modules/UI/Flutter/shell/lib/behaviors/behavior_view_model.dart:38).
- Modules are hard-coded at startup in [DigitalBrainComposition.cs](./src/Kernel/DigitalBrain.Kernel/DigitalBrainComposition.cs:7). They are not dynamically installed runtime plugins.
- Workspace membership and ACL semantics do not yet exist separately from owner identity.
- MAF sessions are persisted only after streaming finishes in [DirectAgentSession.cs](./src/Modules/AI/AI/Orchestration/DirectAgentSession.cs:54).
- The existing Tasks/Execution machinery is not connected to production Conversation turns.
- The Connection lookup performs a linear scan of the durable connection list for each emission and does not validate the complete source/target contract as strongly as MAF validates a Workflow.

So we have a strong kernel direction surrounded by several shallow or aspirational product Modules.

## Recommended architecture

```text
Trusted installed Modules
        │
        ├── provide Neurons, Integrations and capabilities
        │
        ▼
ConnectionGraph
        │ long-lived subscriptions, bindings and triggers
        ▼
BehaviorRevision
        │ versioned bounded program
        ▼
ExecutionNeuron
        │ identity, lifecycle, retries, cancellation,
        │ blockers, operation ledger and durable journal
        ▼
MAF Workflow / direct MAF Agent
        │ Executors use Module capabilities and MCP tools
        ▼
Conversation and Surface projections
```

Important rules:

1. Connections may trigger a Behavior, but must never encode its internal steps.
2. MAF Workflow edges remain private to a Behavior revision.
3. Simple chat uses a direct MAF agent loop—no Workflow required.
4. A repeatable multi-step Behavior may use MAF Workflows.
5. Execution stays provider-neutral and Orleans-owned.
6. MAF checkpoints may be stored through an Orleans adapter.
7. External Gmail/Salesforce effects remain protected by the Execution operation ledger.
8. A Surface is a durable declarative UI document, never a MAF Executor.
9. Modules remain trusted installed code; runtime-generated logic becomes versioned Behavior data/artifacts.
10. We do not add the Durable Extension/DTS until Orleans-backed execution is proven insufficient.

I would also reject the name `DigitalBrainGraph` for the class—it becomes ambiguous immediately. `ConnectionGraphNeuron` or `TopologyGraphNeuron` is more truthful; “Brain Map” can remain the product-facing visualization.

The next ratification question is:

**Do you approve separating `ConnectionGraph` as long-lived product topology from `BehaviorWorkflow` as bounded MAF control flow—and explicitly forbid representing workflow steps as Connections?**

Recommended answer: **approve**.

> **`src/Modules/AI/AI/Orchestration/ModelContracts.cs`** — ModelContracts(class), ContractOf(method), ContractsByModelName(constant), Resolve(method), ModelNameOf(method), LabelFor(method), +3 more

> ```csharp
> 1	using DigitalBrain.Abstractions;
> 2	
> 3	namespace DigitalBrain.AI;
> 4	
> 5	internal static class ModelContracts
> 6	{
> 7	    private static readonly Dictionary<string, Type> ContractsByModelName = Discover();
> 8	
> 9	    internal static Type Resolve(string model)
> 10	    {
> 11	        ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace(model);
> 12	
> 13	        return ContractsByModelName.TryGetValue(model.Trim(), out var contract)
> 14	            ? contract
> 15	            : throw new OrchestrationRefusedException(
> 16	                $"Model '{model}' is not a model this build knows. Known models: {string.Join(", ", KnownModelNames())}. Knowing a model is not the same as it being provisioned here: a known model still fails on its first turn if this deployment has no endpoint or key configured for it.");
> 17	    }
> 18	
> 19	    internal static string ModelNameOf(Type contract)
> 20	    {
> 21	        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(contract);
> 22	
> 23	        return contract.Name[1..];
> 24	    }
> 25	
> 26	    internal static string LabelFor(NeuronId participant)
> 27	        => ContractsByModelName.TryGetValue(participant.Type, out var contract)
> 28	            ? $"{ModelNameOf(contract)} '{participant.Name}'"
> 29	            : $"{participant.Type} '{participant.Name}'";
> 30	
> 31	    internal static IReadOnlyList<string> KnownModelNames()
> 32	        => [.. ContractsByModelName.Keys.Order(StringComparer.Ordinal)];
> 33	
> 34	    private static Dictionary<string, Type> Discover()
> 35	    {
> 36	        var contracts = typeof(ILLM).Assembly.GetExportedTypes();
> 37	        Dictionary<string, Type> byModelName = new(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
> 38	
> 39	        foreach (var model in typeof(LLM).Assembly
> 40	            .GetTypes()
> 41	            .Where(candidate => candidate is { IsClass: true, IsAbstract: false }
> 42	                && candidate.IsSubclassOf(typeof(LLM))))
> 43	        {
> 44	            var contract = ContractOf(model, contracts);
> 45	
> 46	            if (byModelName.TryGetValue(model.Name, out var claimed))
> 47	            {
> 48	                throw new InvalidOperationException(
> 49	                    $"Model name '{model.Name}' is claimed by both '{claimed.FullName}' and '{contract.FullName}'; a model name must select exactly one model.");
> 50	            }
> 51	
> 52	            byModelName.Add(model.Name, contract);
> 53	        }
> 54	
> 55	        return byModelName;
> 56	    }
> 57	
> 58	    private static Type ContractOf(Type model, IReadOnlyList<Type> contracts)
> 59	        => contracts.SingleOrDefault(candidate =>
> 60	            candidate.IsInterface
> 61	            && candidate.Namespace == model.Namespace
> 62	            && string.Equals(candidate.Name, $"I{model.Name}", StringComparison.Ordinal)
> 63	            && typeof(ILLM).IsAssignableFrom(candidate))
> 64	        ?? throw new InvalidOperationException(
> 65	            $"Model '{model.FullName}' has no 'I{model.Name}' contract extending {nameof(ILLM)} in namespace '{model.Namespace}'.");
> 66	}
> ```

> 8	    internal static IReadOnlyList<string> NamedIn(string text, IReadOnlyList<string> known)
> 9	    {
> 10	        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(text);
> 11	        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(known);
> 12	
> 13	        return [.. known.Where(model => IsNamedIn(text, model, known))];
> 14	    }
> 15	
> 16	    private static string FamilyOf(string model)
> 17	    {
> 18	        var letters = 0;
> 19	
> 20	        while (letters < model.Length && char.IsAsciiLetter(model[letters]))
> 21	        {
> 22	            letters++;
> 23	        }
> 24	
> 25	        return letters == 0 ? model : model[..letters];
> 26	    }
> 27	
> 28	    private static bool IsNamedIn(string text, string model, IReadOnlyList<string> known)
> 29	    {
> 30	        var family = FamilyOf(model);
> 31	        var soleModelOfFamily = SoleModelOfFamily(known, family);
> 32	
> 33	        for (var start = text.IndexOf(family, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
> 34	             start >= 0;
> 35	             start = text.IndexOf(family, start + 1, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
> 36	        {
> 37	            var end = start + family.Length;
> 38	
> 39	            while (end < text.Length && char.IsAsciiDigit(text[end]))
> 40	            {
> 41	                end++;
> 42	            }
> 43	
> 44	            if ((start != 0 && char.IsLetterOrDigit(text[start - 1]))
> 45	                || (end != text.Length && char.IsLetterOrDigit(text[end])))
> 46	            {
> 47	                continue;
> 48	            }
> 49	
> 50	            var named = text[start..end];
> 51	            var identifiesThisModel = named.Length == family.Length
> 52	                ? string.Equals(soleModelOfFamily, model, StringComparison.Ordinal)
> 53	                : string.Equals(named, model, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
> 54	
> 55	            if (identifiesThisModel)
> 56	            {
> 57	                return true;
> 58	            }
> 59	        }
> 60	
> 61	        return false;
> 62	    }
> 63	
> 64	    private static string? SoleModelOfFamily(IReadOnlyList<string> known, string family)
> 65	    {
> 66	        string? sole = null;

> 73	            }
> 74	
> 75	            if (sole is not null)

`BehaviorWorkflow` does not exist as a working backend concept today. I introduced it as a proposed architecture. The current Behavior Studio displays demo C# from [behavior_demo_fixtures.dart](./src/Modules/UI/Flutter/shell/lib/behaviors/behavior_demo_fixtures.dart), while [behavior_view_model.dart](./src/Modules/UI/Flutter/shell/lib/behaviors/behavior_view_model.dart) explicitly falls back to fixtures because no Behavior host is composed.

I would refine the name and model:

| Concept | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ConnectionGraph` | Durable topology of the brain: which Neuron receives which emitted fact. |
| `Behavior` | Named, reusable product capability with version history. |
| `BehaviorRevision` | Immutable, approved version of that Behavior. |
| `BehaviorProgram` | What the revision executes: either an agent or an explicit workflow. |
| `WorkflowProgram` | The explicit workflow form, internally executed using MAF. |
| `Execution` | One durable invocation, implemented using the reusable Tasks infrastructure. |

So `BehaviorWorkflow` should become `WorkflowProgram`. It is not another Module, another global graph, or another kind of Synapse.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    T["Timer, user, or Module fact"] -->|"ConnectionGraph"| B["Behavior ingress"]
    B --> E["Execution pins one revision"]
    E --> P{"BehaviorProgram"}
    P -->|"AgentProgram"| A["MAF agent with all actor MCP tools"]
    P -->|"WorkflowProgram"| W["Fresh MAF Workflow"]
    W --> X["Agent, MCP, transform, branch, join executors"]
    A --> O["Typed Behavior output"]
    X --> O
    O -->|"ConnectionGraph"| D["Surface, Conversation, or another Behavior"]
```

The two graphs are complementary:

- ConnectionGraph describes the persistent composition of the product.
- WorkflowProgram describes control flow inside one Behavior.
- A MAF workflow instance executes that program for one Execution.

### Not every Behavior needs a workflow

This is the simplification I was missing earlier:

```text
BehaviorRevision.Program =
    AgentProgram
    or WorkflowProgram
```

An `AgentProgram` is appropriate for:

> “Summarize my unread Gmail and identify important messages.”

It contains instructions, context, and `tools: actor.all`. The agent dynamically chooses from all MCP tools available to the current user, matching your approved MVP policy.

A `WorkflowProgram` is appropriate when the sequence must be visible and repeatable:

> “Every Monday, query Salesforce, enrich the accounts using Gmail and web research, aggregate the pipeline, and update the bar chart.”

Microsoft makes exactly this distinction: agents dynamically choose their steps, while workflows have explicitly defined execution paths. MAF workflows provide typed executors, edges, conditional routing, fan-out/fan-in, events, and checkpointing. [Microsoft Agent Framework workflow overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/workflows/)

### What a WorkflowProgram looks like

The stored artifact should be a small DigitalBrain-owned declarative format:

```yaml
schema: db.behavior/v1
behavior: salesforce-weekly
revision: 3

input: WeeklySalesRequest/v1
output: BarChartSeries/v1

program:
  kind: workflow

  steps:
    - id: load_pipeline
      kind: mcp
      server: salesforce
      tool: query
      arguments:
        query: "current opportunity pipeline"

    - id: enrich
      kind: agent
      instructions: >
        Enrich the accounts with relevant Gmail correspondence
        and web research.
      tools: actor.all

    - id: build_chart
      kind: transform
      operation: group-and-sum
      groupBy: stage
      value: amount

    - id: result
      kind: output
      contract: BarChartSeries/v1

  flows:
    - from: load_pipeline
      to: enrich
    - from: enrich
      to: build_chart
    - from: build_chart
      to: result
```

Its external wiring is separate:

```text
weekly-timer ──Connection──> salesforce-weekly
salesforce-weekly.output ──Connection──> salesforce-weekly-surface.data
```

The Surface owns the bar-chart layout. The Behavior produces `BarChartSeries`; it does not generate Flutter widgets during every run.

There is no `SalesforceReadSynapse`, `GmailReadSynapse`, or special executor class per operation. `salesforce/query` is data inside a generic `McpToolExecutor`. The initial step vocabulary can remain very small:

- `agent`
- `mcp`
- `module`
- `transform`
- `output`

And four flow shapes:

- direct
- conditional/switch
- fan-out
- fan-in/join

No arbitrary loops in v1.

### Where MAF fits

During activation, DigitalBrain validates the revision and its input/output contracts. During execution, a compiler materializes a fresh MAF workflow:

| WorkflowProgram | MAF |
|---|---|
| Step | Executor |
| Direct flow | `AddEdge` |
| Branch | `AddSwitch` or conditional edge |
| Parallel steps | `AddFanOutEdge` |
| Join | `AddFanInBarrierEdge` |
| Result step | `WithOutputFrom` |

The existing [DirectOrchestrationShape.cs](./src/Modules/AI/AI/Orchestration/DirectOrchestrationShape.cs:73) already demonstrates constructing MAF workflows from fresh agents. We would generalize that behind one `BehaviorWorkflowCompiler`, rather than expose `WorkflowBuilder` throughout the system. [MAF WorkflowBuilder documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/workflows/workflows)

MAF would own:

- Step scheduling and message routing.
- Branching and parallel execution.
- Workflow-local state and events.
- Superstep checkpoints.
- Human/external input request points.

DigitalBrain Execution/Tasks would own:

- The pinned `BehaviorRevision`.
- Durable status, retries, cancellation, and attempts.
- OAuth/user-action blockers.
- Stable idempotency identities for external writes.
- Actor identity and Integration credential resolution.
- ConnectionGraph triggers and outputs.

MAF checkpoints do not make a Salesforce write exactly-once, so DigitalBrain must remain the authority for side-effect accounting.

Standard MAF workflows can run in-process with checkpoint storage; they do not require Azure Functions. The separate Durable Extension supports Azure Functions and self-hosted compute, but both use Durable Task infrastructure. We should not adopt it now because it would compete with Orleans/Tasks as the durable execution authority. [MAF Durable Extension](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/integrations/durable-extension)

### How real-time scripting works

1. The user asks the assistant to create or change a Behavior.
2. AI produces `db.behavior/v1` data plus scenarios and a visual diff.
3. DigitalBrain validates contracts, tools, graph structure, and tests.
4. The user approves the immutable revision once.
5. Activation updates the active revision and ConnectionGraph bindings.
6. The Behavior is immediately discoverable and executable—no restart or deployment.
7. Existing executions remain pinned to their old revision.

Flutter can display the same artifact as YAML, a node graph, scenarios, bindings, and a live execution trace.

MAF itself also offers declarative YAML and `InvokeMcpTool`, but I would not make its evolving schema our permanent product storage format. A tiny DigitalBrain schema keeps MAF replaceable while still compiling directly to its execution primitives. [MAF declarative workflows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/workflows/declarative)

Runtime-generated C# should be deferred. Loading generated Roslyn assemblies into the credentialed Orleans process is effectively remote code execution; MAF provides orchestration, not sandboxing. A future `ScriptProgram` can run out-of-process with limited capability RPC.

**Ratification:** do you approve `BehaviorRevision.Program = AgentProgram | WorkflowProgram`, using a small `db.behavior/v1` declarative format compiled to MAF, while deferring generated C# to a later isolated runtime? I recommend approval.

> 44	    {
> 45	        if (participants is null)
> 46	        {
> 47	            throw new InvalidOperationException("Participants returned null.");
> 48	        }
> 49	
> 50	        var snapshot = participants.ToArray();
> 51	
> 52	        if (snapshot.Length == 0)
> 53	        {
> 54	            throw new InvalidOperationException(
> 55	                $"AI orchestration '{orchestration}' requires at least one participant.");
> 56	        }
> 57	
> 58	        if (snapshot.Any(participant => participant is null))
> 59	        {
> 60	            throw new InvalidOperationException(
> 61	                $"AI orchestration '{orchestration}' has a null participant.");
> 62	        }
> 63	
> 64	        if (snapshot.Any(participant => participant.Id.Owner != orchestration.Owner))
> 65	        {
> 66	            throw new InvalidOperationException(
> 67	                $"Every participant in AI orchestration '{orchestration}' must belong to its owner.");
> 68	        }
> 69	
> 70	        return snapshot;
> 71	    }

> 56	    {
> 57	        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(delivery);
> 58	        cancellationToken.ThrowIfCancellationRequested();
> 59	
> 60	        if (delivery.Synapse is AttemptFact fact && delivery.Caller != fact.Worker)
> 61	        {
> 62	            return Task.CompletedTask;
> 63	        }
> 64	
> 65	        if (delivery.Synapse is UserActionRequired)
> 66	        {
> 67	            var data = LoadIfStarted();
> 68	            if (data is null || delivery.Caller != data.Worker)
> 69	            {
> 70	                return Task.CompletedTask;
> 71	            }
> 72	        }
> 73	
> 74	        if (delivery.Synapse is CompleteUserAction or DenyUserAction)
> 75	        {
> 76	            var data = LoadIfStarted();
> 77	            if (data is null)
> 78	            {
> 79	                throw new NeuronAuthorizationException(
> 80	                    $"Caller '{delivery.Caller}' is not the user-action completer for Task '{Id}'.");
> 81	            }
> 82	
> 83	            if (data.Blocker is not UserActionPending pending)
> 84	            {
> 85	                var expectedRevision = delivery.Synapse switch
> 86	                {
> 87	                    CompleteUserAction complete => complete.ExpectedParkRevision,
> 88	                    DenyUserAction deny => deny.ExpectedParkRevision,
> 89	                    _ => -1L,
> 90	                };
> 91	
> 92	                if (data.State is TaskState.Running or TaskState.Pending
> 93	                    && expectedRevision >= 0
> 94	                    && data.Revision == expectedRevision)
> 95	                {
> 96	                    throw new InvalidOperationException(
> 97	                        $"Task '{Id}' is not waiting on a module user action yet.");
> 98	                }
> 99	
> 100	                throw new NeuronAuthorizationException(
> 101	                    $"Caller '{delivery.Caller}' is not the user-action completer for Task '{Id}'.");
> 102	            }
> 103	
> 104	            if (delivery.Caller != pending.Completer)
> 105	            {
> 106	                throw new NeuronAuthorizationException(
> 107	                    $"Caller '{delivery.Caller}' is not the user-action completer for Task '{Id}'.");

> 248	        switch (current, target)
> 249	        {

> 251	                if (responsePayload is not null)
> 252	                {
> 253	                    throw new InvalidOperationException("Prepared→Dispatched cannot carry a response reference.");
> 254	                }
> 255	
> 256	                break;
> 257	
> 258	            case (TaskOperationPhase.Dispatched, TaskOperationPhase.Completed):
> 259	                if (responsePayload is null || responsePayload.Value.Id == Guid.Empty)
> 260	                {
> 261	                    throw new InvalidOperationException("Dispatched→Completed requires a non-empty response reference.");
> 262	                }
> 263	
> 264	                break;
> 265	
> 266	            case (TaskOperationPhase.Dispatched, TaskOperationPhase.Uncertain):
> 267	                if (responsePayload is not null)
> 268	                {
> 269	                    throw new InvalidOperationException("Dispatched→Uncertain cannot carry a response reference.");
> 270	                }
> 271	
> 272	                break;
> 273	
> 274	            default:
> 275	                throw new InvalidOperationException(
> 276	                    $"Transition from '{current}' to '{target}' is not allowed.");
> 277	        }
> 278	    }

> 281	        => left.Target == right.Target
> 282	            && string.Equals(left.RequestSynapseId, right.RequestSynapseId, StringComparison.Ordinal)
> 283	            && left.RequestSchemaVersion == right.RequestSchemaVersion
> 284	            && string.Equals(left.ResponseSynapseId, right.ResponseSynapseId, StringComparison.Ordinal)
> 285	            && left.ResponseSchemaVersion == right.ResponseSchemaVersion;

> 287	    private static BlockerId OperationBlockerId(NeuronId task, AttemptId attempt, int sequence)
> 288	    {
> 289	        var material = $"{task}:{attempt.Value:N}:{sequence.ToString(System.Globalization.CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)}";
> 290	        var hash = SHA256.HashData(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(material));
> 291	        var guidBytes = hash.AsSpan(0, 16).ToArray();
> 292	        if (guidBytes.All(b => b == 0))
> 293	        {
> 294	            guidBytes[^1] = 1;
> 295	        }
> 296	
> 297	        return new BlockerId(new Guid(guidBytes));
> 298	    }
> 299	}

> 167	    private static double Cosine(float[] left, float[] right)
> 168	    {
> 169	        if (left.Length != right.Length || left.Length == 0)
> 170	        {
> 171	            return 0;
> 172	        }
> 173	
> 174	        double dot = 0, leftLength = 0, rightLength = 0;
> 175	        for (var index = 0; index < left.Length; index++)
> 176	        {
> 177	            dot += (double)left[index] * right[index];
> 178	            leftLength += (double)left[index] * left[index];
> 179	            rightLength += (double)right[index] * right[index];
> 180	        }
> 181	
> 182	        return leftLength == 0 || rightLength == 0
> 183	            ? 0
> 184	            : dot / (Math.Sqrt(leftLength) * Math.Sqrt(rightLength));
> 185	    }

> 188	    {
> 189	        var matched = query.Count(entry.Haystack.Contains);
> 190	        return matched == 0 ? 0 : (double)matched / query.Count;
> 191	    }

> 193	    internal static IReadOnlyCollection<string> Tokens(string text)
> 194	    {
> 195	        var tokens = new HashSet<string>(StringComparer.Ordinal);
> 196	        var word = new StringBuilder();
> 197	
> 198	        void Cut()
> 199	        {
> 200	            if (word.Length > 2)
> 201	            {
> 202	                tokens.Add(word.ToString());
> 203	            }
> 204	
> 205	            word.Clear();
> 206	        }
> 207	
> 208	        foreach (var letter in text)
> 209	        {
> 210	            if (char.IsLetterOrDigit(letter))
> 211	            {
> 212	                if (char.IsUpper(letter) && word.Length > 0 && !char.IsUpper(word[^1]))
> 213	                {
> 214	                    Cut();
> 215	                }
> 216	
> 217	                word.Append(char.ToLowerInvariant(letter));
> 218	                continue;
> 219	            }
> 220	
> 221	            Cut();
> 222	        }
> 223	
> 224	        Cut();
> 225	        return tokens;
> 226	    }
